analysis: Frame 7 of the data set (single-storey two-bay frame with a diagonal brace and a lean-on column), units kip and inch. Plane frame in the global X-Y plane (Y vertical); the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held (the data set's frames are 'fully braced out-of-plane'); in-plane bending about local z, so the data set's Izz is the section's Iz. Modulus 0.8 E = 23200 ksi (the data set's condition for all elastic analyses; its element table points to E = 29000 ksi, the published results correspond to 0.8 E - verified for this frame with the first-order displacements). No shear deformation. A straight line of the data set's elements is one member here, the loads at its interior nodes are point loads on the member. The data set's model is plane (no out-of-plane buckling of a member between joints); the engine's member is spatial, so Iy = 1000 Izz is entered for every section instead of the listed Iyy: no out-of-plane mode can precede the in-plane behaviour compared, and Iy does not enter the in-plane results. Case 'Left' of the data set: imperfect geometry with every node at x - y/500, lateral loads acting toward -x (gravity loads unchanged). Second-order elastic analysis, compared with the data set's 'WC' results: MASTAN2, work-control incremental analysis with step size 0.001, updated Lagrangian formulation with geometric stiffness matrices, 4 elements per member (article, Tables 2 and 3). The engine solves the small-displacement second-order theory with exact member stability functions (docs/THEORY.md 10, 12).

quarantine.diagnosis: 3 of 4 targets missed: joints 14 and 18 by 5e-4 and 1.3e-3 relative (engine -2.4002 and -2.4059 in, data set -2.398659 and -2.408860), joint 29 by 3.0e-2 (engine -0.1891, data set -0.1947 in; a small displacement of the braced bay). Cause: different theory. The data set's WC values come from MASTAN2's incremental work-control analysis (step 0.001) in an updated Lagrangian formulation, 4 elements per member: a large-displacement analysis. The engine solves the classical small-displacement second-order theory (P-Delta and P-delta with exact stability functions; docs/THEORY.md 10 and 12), which neglects terms of second order in the kinematics such as the shortening of the chord of a bent member. Evidence (verification/derive/ziemian_diagnosis.py, case 'Right', joint displacements): OpenSeesPy with the linearised 'PDelta' transformation, 32 elements per member, agrees with the engine within (case 'Right' not solvable by the engine, see frame-7-second-order-right; for the other frames 3e-5 ... 3e-4); OpenSeesPy with the 'Corotational' (large-displacement) transformation agrees with the data set within 1.1e-3 (32 elements per member; 1.3e-3 with the data set's own 4 elements per member), while the engine differs from the data set by up to 3.0e-2 (case 'Left'). The remaining difference between the corotational results and the data set (element formulation, increment size) was not resolved. The targets are outside what the engine's theory can reproduce at the printed precision; they are kept, evaluated and reported, and never counted as passed.
